description:
Carved out of `JMAP-g7wu.2.4.2`: count-limit enforcement for `Space/set` add* operations.

Per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space/set (revised 2026-05-11, spec commit `80d5e11`), each of the four add* ops MUST return an `overQuota` SetError (RFC 8620 §5.3) when the resulting count would exceed a server-defined limit:

- `addRoles` — roles per Space
- `addMembers` — members per Space
- `addChannels` — channels per Space
- `addCategories` — categories per Space

The cap values are implementation-defined — the current spec does not define named capability fields for them. Per-aggregate enforcement happens at `Space/set` time before the mutation is applied. Account-level cap visibility to clients (when wanted) is a separate future path via JMAP Quotas (RFC 9425).

## Implementation sketch

1. Add `ChatLimits` struct + `ChatBackend::limits(&self, caller, account_id) -> ChatLimits` method to `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs`. Sync default impl returning const-fixed values. See workspace `AGENTS.md` "Backend caps and limits" for the canonical cross-extension pattern.

2. In `handle_space_set` (`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs`), after parsing ops and before `backend.apply_space_patch()`:
   - Group add* ops by collection (roles / members / channels / categories)
   - Query current Space counts via the backend
   - Compare (existing + add) against the relevant `ChatLimits` field
   - Reject the entire add* entry with `overQuota` if any aggregate would exceed its cap (entry-level atomicity, matching RFC 8620 §5.3 `/set` semantics at the target level)

Detailed design decisions (`ChatLimits` struct shape, default values, sync signature, caller/account_id plumbing) are in the NOTES section below.

## Out of scope

- Group `Chat/set` membership cap enforcement (spec mandates `overQuota` there too; separate bead if/when wanted).
- Per-message caps (`maxBodyBytes`, `maxAttachmentBytes`, `maxAttachmentsPerMessage`) — those remain on the chat capability per RFC 8621 analog and are enforced at message-parse time, not `Space/set` time.
- Client-side cap visibility via JMAP Quotas (`urn:ietf:params:jmap:quotas`) — not yet implemented in the workspace.

Deferred from `JMAP-g7wu.2.4.2` because no infrastructure existed and the design question (where the cap values live) was open. Resolved 2026-05-11 (option c, backend-owned via `ChatBackend::limits()`).
notes:
Decision (2026-05-11, Mark): no longer human-blocked. The JMAP-ga0q architectural decision establishes 'backend is canonical for enforcement' as workspace policy. Count-limit enforcement (maxRolesPerSpace, maxSpaceMembers, maxChannelsPerSpace, maxCategoriesPerSpace) is pure state-count enforcement with no identity dependency; backend reads current counts and rejects if a patch would exceed any limit.

This bead is implementation-only and the autonomous /do-beads loop can pick it up after JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 lands (so the gating + count-check paths can share the same patch-application loop in apply_space_patch).

Soft dependency on .4.3 added below (not a hard blocks-link; .8 could land in parallel but is cleaner co-located).
Decision (2026-05-11, Mark): go with all bot recommendations.

1. **Configuration shape: (c)** — `ChatBackend::limits() -> ChatLimits` method on the backend trait. Matches Email/import precedent in jmap-mail-server. Backend owns the policy; handler queries once per request and compares (existing_count + add_count) > cap.

2. **Signature: sync** with default impl returning const-fixed values. Backends that need per-tenant lookup cache at construction time. Future API break to async is possible under #[non_exhaustive] traits if ever needed.

3. **Default values** (in the trait's default impl):
   - max_roles_per_space = 50
   - max_space_members = 10_000
   - max_channels_per_space = 500
   - max_categories_per_space = 100

4. **Atomicity: entry-level reject-all.** If a single add* entry would push the collection over cap, reject all entries in that add op with the appropriate over-quota SetError. Matches RFC 8620 /set atomicity model.

ChatLimits struct shape (bead claimant may refine, but this is the intended baseline):

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ChatLimits {
    pub max_roles_per_space: u32,
    pub max_space_members: u32,
    pub max_channels_per_space: u32,
    pub max_categories_per_space: u32,
}

impl Default for ChatLimits {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            max_roles_per_space: 50,
            max_space_members: 10_000,
            max_channels_per_space: 500,
            max_categories_per_space: 100,
        }
    }
}
```

And on ChatBackend:

```rust
fn limits(&self) -> ChatLimits {
    ChatLimits::default()
}
```

Autonomous /do-beads loop now owns the implementation. Soft co-location with JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 (apply_space_patch enforcement) remains a preference but not a hard block — both can land in either order.
Spec posture revision (2026-05-11, Mark): the spec edit that JMAP-kt5k tracks REMOVES the cap-advertising fields from accountCapabilities["urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat"] entirely. The implementation decision recorded above stays correct in shape but changes in framing:

  - Was: 'spec-mandated enforcement of named caps (maxRolesPerSpace, maxSpaceMembers, maxChannelsPerSpace, maxCategoriesPerSpace) defined in account capability'
  - Now: 'implementation-defined per-Space content limits exposed via ChatBackend::limits(), with no spec contract on specific values or client-visible advertisement'

The implementation work (struct shape, sync default method, bot's numeric defaults, entry-level reject-all atomicity) is unchanged. No session-capability advertisement work is needed — there is no cap field in the session capability to populate. JMAP Quota integration (if/when the workspace implements urn:ietf:params:jmap:quotas) becomes the future path for client-visible cap exposure, separately from this bead.

## Trait signature amendment (workspace policy fix)

The original decision specified `fn limits(&self) -> ChatLimits` with no args. That was incomplete — it precluded per-caller / per-account customization without a future API break. The corrected signature accepts caller and account_id even though the default impl ignores them:

```rust
fn limits(&self, _caller: &Self::CallerCtx, _account_id: &jmap_types::Id) -> ChatLimits {
    ChatLimits::default()
}
```

This becomes the cross-extension workspace pattern: any extension server that grows caps adds an `XxxLimits` struct + a sync trait method `fn limits(&self, caller, account_id) -> XxxLimits` with const-default-impl values overridable per-backend. Mail-server's existing per-method `max_<thing>(caller, account_id)` shape is older and not retroactively re-shaped without a deliberate consolidation bead.

The autonomous /do-beads loop continues to own this bead with the amended signature. Cross-reference to JMAP-kt5k for the spec edit Mark is doing in parallel.
Workspace policy lifted (2026-05-11, Mark): the cross-extension cap pattern recorded in this bead's notes is now codified in workspace AGENTS.md 'Backend caps and limits' section (lines 404-462). Future extension authors growing caps consult that section rather than re-deriving the pattern from this bead.
title: Count-limit enforcement for handle_space_set (roles / members / channels / categories per Space)
